Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 11944 - 1987 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
WALLET, LEATHER 

0* FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 24 March 1987, after the draft finalized by the Travel 
Requisites Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer 
Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 

0.2 In the preparation of this standard due weightage has been given to 
the proper type of materials to be used and prevalent trade practices 
being followed by the manufacturers in this field. 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accord- 
ance with IS ; 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 



1* SCOPE 

1,1 This standard covers requirements for leather wallet. 

2. SHAPE, DESIGN AND DIMENSIONS 

2.1 The wallet shall be manufactured to the shape, design and dimensions 
as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. A typical design is, 
however, shown in Fig. I. 

2.1*1 A deviation of ±2'5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions 
in Fig. 1. 

3. MATERIALS 

3,1 Body — Suitable vegetable, chrome or combination tanned sheep, 

cow or young buffalo leather shall be used for the manufacture of the 

wallet. 

3*2 Sewing Thread — Cotton sevv'ing thread conforming to variety 

No. 5, 14 or 19 of IS : 1720-1978t shall be used for stitching the wallet. 

♦Rules for rounding olT numerical values ( revised ). 
fSpecification for cotton sewing threads ( second revision ). 

3 



^1, ^ 




P == Pocket 

All dimensions in millimetres. 

Fig. 1 A Tvpjcal Wallet 



IS: 11944- 1987 

4. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4.1 The stitching shall be single row stitch with 28 to 32 stitches per 
decimetre of even tension. The loose ends of the thread shall be 
trimmed. 

4.2 The wallet shall be soundly constructed and finished smooth without 
any constructional defects. 

4.3 In respect of appearance, general workmanship and finish, the 
wallet shall conform to the sample previously approved by the buyer. 

5. SAMPLING 

5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, 
the procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )'1973* shall be followed for 
sampling. The sampling plan and the inspection level as given in 5.2 
and 5.3 shall be followed^ 

5.2 The scale of sampling shall correspond to Inspection Level III 
given in Table 1 of IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1973* for all the requirements 
mentioned in this specification. 

5.3 The sampling plan shall correspond to AQL plans of 4 percent 
given in Table 2 of IS : 2500 ( Part 1 )-I973*. 

6. MARKING 

6.1 Each wallet shall be legibly marked with the manufacturer's name 
or trade-mark and batch number. 

6.1.1 Each wallet may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 

Note — The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance 
that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard 
under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised 
and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products 
are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further 
safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard 
Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7. PACKING 

7.1 The wallets shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 

♦Sampling inspection tables: Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of 
defects (first revision ).
